questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cure a cold quickly with simple home remedies
Why flu is more dangerous in winter than in summer
How hormones control our moods and our energy
Whether men really suffer more from colds and flu
questions.why: Dan says it's about 'man flu' and whether it's real or just something men complain about.

questions.q: How does Dan react when Neil says he's getting something serious?
options: He sends Neil home to rest for the rest of the day
He says it's only a cold and Neil should keep going
He agrees that Neil looks very ill and should see a doctor
He offers to do the whole programme alone today
questions.why: Dan calls it 'just a case of the sniffles' and says Neil will have to soldier on.

questions.q: What do the British couple think about 'man flu'?
options: They both think it is real and men suffer more
They both think men just complain more than women
He thinks men suffer more; she thinks they complain more
She thinks women suffer more; he isn't sure either way
questions.why: The man says men 'definitely do suffer a lot more'; the woman feels 'they just complain more'.

questions.q: What example does the British woman give?
options: She still went to work when ill, but Chris stayed on the sofa
Chris went to work when he was ill, but she stayed in bed
They were both ill at the same time and both stayed at home
Chris never gets ill, even when everyone else in the house does
questions.why: She says she carried on and went to work, while Chris was on the sofa and couldn't do anything.

questions.q: What has the Dutch woman accused her boyfriend of?
options: Pretending to be ill to miss work
Complaining again and again
Refusing to see a doctor
Giving her his cold
questions.why: She says she accused him of 'whining'.

questions.q: What does Dr Kyle Sue suggest about hormones and infections?
options: Oestrogen makes infections last longer
Hormones have no effect on illness
Men and women have exactly the same hormones
More testosterone means a weaker immune response
questions.why: He says the higher the testosterone, the lower the immune response; oestrogen does the opposite.

questions.q: What does the Royal College of GPs in the UK say?
options: There is no such thing as 'man flu'
'Man flu' is a serious illness
Women complain more than men
Dr Sue's study has proved 'man flu' is real
questions.why: Dan says the Royal College of GPs says there is no such thing as 'man flu'.

questions.q: Why does Dan tell Neil to 'hold his horses'?
options: Neil is speaking too fast for the listeners
Neil wants to go home early to rest in bed
The evidence doesn't prove 'man flu' is real yet
Neil has forgotten to answer the quiz question
questions.why: Dan says even Dr Sue admits the results are only 'suggestive', not 'definitive', and more studies are needed.
